STEP 1 - Vessel type: shallow-to-deep bowl, white interior visible at the rim, curved wall, food mound sits near the rim. Call it a serving/salad bowl with a fairly full heap.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type cue: serving bowl 20-25 cm.
b) Reference object: grapes are about 2.2 cm. Across the bowl, roughly 11-12 grapes fit side by side across the full diameter (the bowl spans about 250 px, a grape about 22-24 px), so width ≈ 11.5 × 2.2 ≈ 25 cm.
Reconciled width: about 24 cm.

STEP 3 - Food item: grapes (dark red, whole).
- Capacity: 0.35 × 24³ / 1000 = 0.35 × 13.8 / 1 ≈ 4.8 L.
- Fill: food sits near the rim with a slight heap, so fill ≈ 0.9 of depth.
- Food volume: 4.8 × 0.9 × 0.9 ≈ 3.9 L = 3900 ml.
- Grapes are whole fruit, so use the countable-piece route as a check: the visible surface shows about 45 grapes, and roughly 2 layers deep hides about as many again, so about 90 grapes × 5 g = 450 g.
- Volume route: 3900 ml × 0.6 (chopped/whole fruit bulk density, with air gaps between whole grapes) ≈ 2300 g, which overshoots. Whole grapes pack loosely, so the count route is more reliable for this item. Take about 450 g, adjusted up slightly for the heap to about 500 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: grapes fill the bowl below the surface, already included in the layer count. No separate base layer.

STEP 5 - Grapes: about 69 kcal per 100 g (raw/as served).
Energy: 500 g × 0.69 ≈ 345 kcal.
